stepNotes.1: Auth owns schema-checked credential CRUD in index.ts and versioned field encryption plus canaries in encryption.ts.
stepNotes.2: The material boundaries are plaintext-to-disk encryption, installation-secret availability, corrupt records, and cross-process lock ownership.
stepNotes.3: Mutations fail closed on corrupt JSON, migration compares a fresh locked read byte-for-byte, and stale lock deletion revalidates its claimed snapshot.
stepNotes.4: PBKDF2 cost is amortized by installation-secret caching and coalesced all() reads; whole-file mutation is suitable for a small credential map.
stepNotes.5: Crypto and persistence/locking responsibilities are separated, with Instance supplying lifecycle-scoped cache ownership.
stepNotes.6: No implementation TODOs or empty catches were found; the only reset export is explicitly test-only and exercised.
stepNotes.7: Encryption and auth tests cover fallback warnings, corruption, canaries, fresh/stale locks, and concurrent migration; true multi-process contention remains a gap.
stepNotes.8: AUTH-001/002/003 remain verified-fixed, no new finding was accepted, and no Critical re-verification file applies.
stepNotes.9: The combined auth/config run passed 186 tests and the core TypeScript check passed.
